intro.definition: An AI technique that enhances Large Language Models by retrieving relevant information from external knowledge bases before generating responses. In 2026, almost every frontier model does this — often as hidden tool calls we call partial retrieval.
intro.paperTitle: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
intro.explanation: Unlike traditional LLMs that rely only on training data, RAG fetches relevant documents at query time — enabling accurate, up-to-date, and verifiable responses.

introScreen.lede: RAG — Retrieval-Augmented Generation — is the idea of letting a model look things up before it answers. What started as a 2020 research paper is now the invisible backbone of Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and every agentic workflow you use. We call the modern form partial retrieval: small, on-demand lookups hidden inside tool calls.
introScreen.visibleBody: You pick a document. You see it split into chunks, turned into vectors, searched by meaning, and stitched into a prompt. Nothing is hidden — you can inspect every step on your own machine.
introScreen.hiddenBody: When Claude searches the web, reads a file, runs code, or recalls a memory, it is performing the same pipeline: embed a query, retrieve relevant context, then continue generating. The UI often shows only the final answer — not the retrieval that shaped it.
introScreen.insightLine: If you understand these 5 steps, you understand how today's AI gets its facts.
introScreen.insightBody: The model in front of you is not a database. It is a generator wrapped around a silent retrieval loop. The quality of any answer is largely the quality of what got retrieved — and whether the retrieval happened at all.

epilogue.title: Epilogue
epilogue.description: Partial Retrieval — the hidden RAG inside modern AI

epilogue.title: Every frontier AI does this — usually without telling you.
epilogue.lede: You just stepped through the classic pipeline. Here is where the same five moves hide inside the products you use every day, often as tool calls you never see.
epilogue.samePipelineBody: Modern agents don't present retrieval as a separate stage. The model decides mid-answer when it needs more context, fires a tool call, receives partial context back, and continues. That is still RAG — just invisible, adaptive, and plural.

pipeline.uploadHidden: The web, your files, memory, docs
pipeline.chunkHidden: Done by the retrieval tool, not you
pipeline.retrieveHidden: Triggered by a tool call mid-answer

epilogue.productsLede: Transparency varies. Some products surface retrieval clearly; most surface only the answer.

products.claude: Claude's web_search, file_search, and code_execution tools each perform targeted retrieval. You see a tool-use indicator, but rarely the full set of chunks that actually landed in context.
products.chatgpt: ChatGPT Search grounds answers on live web results. Projects and long-term memory inject older context via embeddings and summaries — often without a visible retrieval step.
products.gemini: Gemini can ground responses on Google Search. The model decides when grounding happens; citations are surfaced, but the intermediate retrievals usually are not.
products.perplexity: Perplexity shows its sources up front — the clearest example of visible, citation-first RAG as a product.
products.code: Cursor, Claude Code, and similar IDE agents run retrieval over your codebase using grep, file reads, and embeddings. They typically show the files they touched but not the ranking that selected them.
products.agents: Agent frameworks (tool-use, MCP, function calling) treat retrieval as just another tool. The model chooses when and what to fetch, so retrieval is partial, dynamic, and per-turn.

epilogue.takeaway1Body: If retrieval is partial, citations aren't optional. Push every factual claim back to a source the model actually retrieved.
epilogue.takeaway2Body: Modern models retrieve silently. Good or bad answers often reflect what the retrieval tool saw — not the model's raw capability.
epilogue.takeaway3Label: Treat the prompt as a stage
epilogue.takeaway3Body: The final prompt is what the model actually reads. Everything else — memory, search, files — exists to shape that prompt.
epilogue.closingTitle: Knowing the pipeline makes you a better AI user.
epilogue.closingBody: You can now reason about why an answer is good or bad, when retrieval probably fired, what context it likely landed, and where a system is hiding its sources. That is the real superpower of understanding RAG in 2026.

education.ragExplanation: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) is like giving an AI a textbook before an exam. Instead of guessing from memory, the AI can look up the answer in YOUR documents. This makes responses accurate, verifiable, and grounded in facts.
education.step1: 1. UPLOAD: Your document becomes the AI's reference material
education.step2: 2. CHUNK: Split into searchable pieces (too big = slow, too small = loses context)
education.step3: 3. EMBED: Convert to meaning-vectors (similar meanings = similar numbers)
education.step4: 4. RETRIEVE: Find the chunks closest to your question
education.step5: 5. GENERATE: AI answers using ONLY the relevant context
